topics.concept: BPMN uses standard shapes for events, tasks, gateways, and flows so any reader can follow a process the same way. An ASCII modeler renders these shapes in text: rounded boxes for tasks, diamonds for decisions, arrows for sequence flows. It brings diagram discipline to environments where drawing tools are unavailable.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded process definitions with tasks, gateways, and events, validates the flow for dead ends, and renders the ASCII BPMN-style diagram.
topics.name: ASCII BPMN Flow Modeler
topics.real_world_use: Analysts sketch process flows in ASCII during workshops before formal modeling.

topics.concept: SIPOC names the suppliers, inputs, process steps, outputs, and customers of a process on one page. It bounds the improvement effort: everything outside the SIPOC is out of scope. The generator assembles the five columns from a process brief and checks that every output has a customer.
topics.data_idea: Takes seeded process briefs, generates the five SIPOC columns, and validates that inputs come from named suppliers and outputs reach named customers.
topics.name: SIPOC Diagram Generator
topics.real_world_use: Six Sigma teams start every improvement project with a SIPOC to agree on scope.

topics.concept: A RACI matrix assigns each activity one accountable owner, responsible doers, consulted parties, and informed watchers. Exactly one accountable per row is the rule that prevents diffusion of ownership. The builder assembles the matrix and flags rows with zero or multiple accountable owners.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded activities and roles, builds the RACI matrix, and validates the one-accountable rule plus workload balance across roles.
topics.name: RACI Matrix Builder
topics.real_world_use: Project managers publish RACI matrices so everyone knows who decides and who does.

topics.concept: Swimlane diagrams place each process step in the lane of the role or system that performs it, making handoffs visible. Every lane crossing is a potential delay and a place where work gets dropped. The mapper renders lanes in text and counts handoffs as a complexity metric.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded cross-functional processes with steps assigned to lanes, renders the ASCII swimlanes, and reports handoff counts and wait-prone crossings.
topics.name: Swimlane Process Mapper
topics.real_world_use: Operations teams map swimlanes to find handoffs that slow order fulfillment.

topics.concept: A process glossary defines the nouns of a workflow: what counts as an order, a case, or a completed step. Fuzzy definitions let two teams measure the same process differently. The glossary builder collects candidate terms from process descriptions and drafts shared definitions.
topics.data_idea: Scans seeded process descriptions for domain nouns, proposes definitions, and flags terms defined differently across documents.

key_params.min_mentions: occurrences to qualify as a term

topics.name: Process Glossary Builder
topics.real_world_use: Process offices maintain glossaries so metrics mean the same thing enterprise-wide.

topics.concept: A lightweight value stream sketch lists the steps from request to delivery with the time each step adds versus the time work waits. The ratio of value time to total lead time is usually shockingly low. Even a rough sketch points improvement effort at the waiting, not the working.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded process steps with touch time and wait time, computes the value ratio, and renders a simple lead-time sketch.
topics.name: Value Stream Sketch
topics.real_world_use: Lean teams sketch value streams in kaizen events to target waiting waste.

topics.concept: Five whys digs past symptoms by asking why repeatedly until a root cause surfaces. The discipline is answering with facts at each level, not jumping to blame. A logger structures the chain, records the evidence per why, and stops when the cause is actionable.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded problem statements with symptom chains, guides the five-level drill-down, and validates that each level is supported by evidence.
topics.name: Five Whys Root Cause Logger
topics.real_world_use: Quality teams log five-whys chains in incident reviews to prevent repeat failures.

topics.concept: A full value stream map adds data boxes to every step: cycle time, changeover time, uptime, and inventory between steps. It quantifies the current state so the future state can be designed, not wished. The map also separates value-adding steps from the necessary and pure waste.
topics.data_idea: Generates a seeded production process with per-step metrics and inter-step inventory, computes total lead time versus value time, and renders the annotated map.
topics.name: Value Stream Mapper
topics.real_world_use: Manufacturers map value streams to plan lead-time reduction programs.

topics.concept: A bottleneck is the step with the lowest throughput: it sets the pace of the whole process no matter how fast everything else runs. Utilization near 100 percent with growing queues marks it. The finder computes capacity per step from cycle times and resources, then ranks constraints.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded multi-step processes with cycle times and staffing, computes utilization and queue buildup per step, and identifies the binding constraint.
topics.name: Process Bottleneck Finder
topics.real_world_use: Operations managers find bottlenecks before buying capacity they do not need.

topics.concept: Cycle time analysis breaks lead time into processing, waiting, and rework components per step. Waiting usually dominates, which means capacity is rarely the real problem. The analyzer quantifies each component and shows where a small change buys the most time.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded case histories with timestamps per step, decomposes cycle time into components, and ranks steps by waiting-time contribution.
topics.name: Cycle Time Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Service operations teams analyze cycle time to cut customer wait in claims and onboarding.

topics.concept: Process costing assigns labor, material, and overhead to each step so the true cost of the process is visible. Steps that consume the most cost per unit of value become redesign candidates. The model rolls step costs up to a cost-per-case figure finance can trust.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded step costs with labor rates and overhead drivers, computes cost per step and per completed case, and ranks steps by cost intensity.
topics.name: Process Step Costing Model
topics.real_world_use: Shared-services leaders cost processes to price internal chargebacks fairly.

topics.concept: Tollgates are phase-end reviews where a project must meet criteria to proceed: scope defined, risks assessed, business case approved. A checker scores each gate's evidence against its criteria and blocks passage on red items. It enforces discipline without turning reviews into theater.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded project phases with gate criteria and evidence, scores each gate, and produces a pass, conditional, or stop verdict with reasons.
topics.name: Phase Tollgate Checker
topics.real_world_use: PMOs run tollgate reviews to stop weak projects before they consume budgets.

topics.concept: A spaghetti diagram traces the physical path of people, materials, or documents through a workspace. Tangled lines expose wasted motion that time studies miss. The simulator replays seeded movement paths on a grid and measures total travel distance.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded worker and material paths on a facility grid, renders the tangled ASCII paths, and computes travel distance before and after a layout change.
topics.name: Spaghetti Diagram Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Warehouse teams redraw layouts after spaghetti diagrams reveal wasted travel.

topics.concept: Queueing models predict waiting from arrival rates and service times: when utilization approaches one, queues explode nonlinearly. The simulator runs arrivals and servers over time and reports average wait, queue length, and server idle time. It answers how many servers a target wait time really needs.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded arrivals with Poisson-like timing and service times across server counts, then reports wait statistics and the servers needed for a wait target.
topics.name: Queueing Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Call centers size staffing from queueing math to hit service-level targets.

topics.concept: Discrete-event simulation advances a clock from event to event: arrivals, service completions, and breakdowns. It captures interactions that averages hide, like a breakdown during a rush hour. The model reports throughput, utilization, and wait distributions across replications for statistical confidence.
topics.data_idea: Runs seeded event-driven process models with stochastic arrivals and failures across replications, and reports confidence intervals on throughput and wait.
topics.name: Discrete Event Process Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Industrial engineers validate factory designs with discrete-event simulation before building.

topics.concept: A what-if capacity planner asks how the process behaves if demand doubles, a shift is added, or a step is automated. It reruns the capacity model under each scenario and reports utilization, queues, and cost. Decisions about hiring and equipment become experiments instead of guesses.
topics.data_idea: Takes a seeded baseline process model, applies scenario changes to demand and capacity, and compares utilization, queue, and cost outcomes per scenario.
topics.name: Capacity What-If Planner
topics.real_world_use: Capacity planners test growth scenarios before committing to hires or equipment.

topics.concept: Process mining reconstructs the real process from event logs: which paths cases actually took, where they looped, and how long each variant lasted. The discovered model almost always differs from the documented one. The lite version builds the variant map and conformance gaps from seeded logs.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded event logs with case IDs, activities, and timestamps including deviant paths, discovers process variants, and reports conformance to the intended model.
topics.name: Process Mining Lite
topics.real_world_use: Enterprises mine ERP logs to find how purchasing really happens versus policy.

topics.concept: An SLA breach predictor watches live case age, queue depth, and step dwell times to forecast which cases will miss their deadlines. Early warnings let teams expedite or reassign before the breach. The model learns breach signatures from historical case data.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded case histories with breach outcomes, trains a simple predictor on age and queue features, and scores live cases for breach risk.
topics.name: SLA Breach Predictor
topics.real_world_use: Operations centers predict SLA breaches to intervene while recovery is still possible.

topics.concept: Lean waste auditing walks a process hunting the classic wastes: waiting, overproduction, defects, motion, and excess processing. Each finding gets a type, a location, and an estimated cost. The audit report ranks wastes by savings potential so improvement starts where it pays.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded process observations with waste instances, classifies each by waste type, estimates cost impact, and ranks findings by savings.
topics.name: Lean Waste Auditor
topics.real_world_use: Continuous-improvement teams audit wastes quarterly to feed kaizen pipelines.

topics.concept: Automation ROI ranking scores candidate processes on volume, rule clarity, error cost, and implementation effort. High-volume, rules-based, error-prone work tops the list. The ranker computes payback per candidate so the automation roadmap funds itself in order.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded catalog of automation candidates with volume and complexity data, scores each on ROI factors, and produces a ranked roadmap with payback periods.
topics.name: Automation ROI Ranker
topics.real_world_use: Digital transformation offices rank automation candidates to sequence RPA investments.
